 Halloween festival cancelled by storm after one night of macabre mayhem 
 Image source, Jamie Simpson/Renfrewshire Council 
 Image caption, Hundreds of performers took part in the parade on the first night of the festival
 By Rachel Grant BBC Scotland 
 Published
 7 hours ago 
 Storm forecasts have led to the cancellation of festivities in "Scotland's Halloween capital" this weekend. 
 The annual event in Paisley, Renfrewshire went ahead on Friday with more than 400 performers, but the Saturday festivities have been called off.
 Organisers at Renfrewshire Council said they were "very sorry" and tickets for grandstand seating would be refunded.
 Paisley has developed a reputation for its playful take on the macabre , linked by some to the darker aspects of the history of Paisley.
 Council officials claim the town has the unofficial title of "Scotland's Halloween capital", with the annual two-day Halloween festival involving a parade, street theatre and a funfair.
 Image source, Jamie Simpson/Renfrewshire Council 
 Image caption, The town was dressed in its spooky best with monster installations and eerie lighting displays on some of the town's most well-known buildings
 Thousands of spectators turned out on Friday as Paisley was transformed into a spine-tingling spectacle of light, music and street theatre at the free event in the town centre streets.
 Hundreds of professional and local community performers marched in the highlight of the event - the Halloween parade, which brought this year's Haunted House theme to life.
 However, the second night of the event will not be happening because of the high winds predicted when Storm Boelo hits the west of Scotland later .
 Most of the country is now covered by a yellow Met Office warning until Saturday, while a more severe amber alert takes effect from 21:00 on Saturday until 21:00 on Sunday, covering the mainland and Western Isles.
 Image source, Jamie Simpson/Renfrewshire Council 
 Image caption, The Halloween parade brought this year's Haunted House theme to life on Friday
 Forecasters say the storm, which is the second named storm in two days, could result in injury, flying debris, power cuts and damage to trees and buildings.
 Lucy Adamson, Renfrewshire Council's head of marketing, communications and events, said: "Unfortunately, a forecast for severe weather means we have decided to cancel today's events at the Paisley Halloween Festival.
 "We're very sorry for any inconvenience caused but public safety is our priority, and we want our events to be safe and enjoyable for everyone.
 "Anyone who purchased tickets for the grandstand seating for tonight's event will be refunded and will be contacted directly by email.
 Image source, Jamie Simpson/Renfrewshire Council 
 Image caption, Hundreds of professional and local community performers took part
 Image source, Jamie Simpson/Renfrewshire Council 
 Paisley held the last known mass execution for witchcraft in western Europe in the late 17th Century.
 Seven people, four women, a man and two boys aged 11 and 14 stood trial and were found guilty.
 After they were hanged and their bodies burned, their mass grave was sealed with a horseshoe, and a myth soon grew that should the horseshoe be disturbed then the whole town would suffer.
 It was later moved by roadworks in the 1960s - a time when Paisley's engineering and famous textile industry were in decline.
 Image source, Jamie Simpson/Renfrewshire Council 
 Image source, Jamie Simpson/Renfrewshire Council
